UNDER SECTION 355 OF Cr.P.C.
 1.
Sl. No. of the case C.C.No.24098/2016 Date of commission of the 2. 01.12.2011 to 08.08.2015 offence (As per F.I.R.) Jayanagar Police Station,
3. Name of the complainant Bengaluru City Dayananda Prabhu, S/o Late Prabhu, Aged about 48 years, R/at No.201, 3rd D Cross,
4.

Name of the accused 7th Main Road, Maruthi Layout, Subramanyapura Post, Uttarahalli,
Bengaluru-61.
5. The offences complained Sections 420, 465 and 471 of of the Indian Penal Code 6. Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty 7.
Final order The accused is acquitted 8.
Date of order 14.08.2024
The Police Sub-Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru City has filed Police Report against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

1 2.
It is the case of the Prosecution that the informant is the Branch Manager of Indian Bank.
This informant has contented that their Bank is a nationalized Bank constituted under Banking Companies Act of 1970.
They are having one of the Branches at Jayanagar, Bengaluru.
During the month of November 2011 the accused had applied for loan of Rs.15,00,000/- in the name of M/s.D.P.Foods.

The accused has furnished the audited Balance Sheet for the year of 31.03.2009,
31.03.2010 and of 31.03.2011 in the name of M/s.D.P.Foods.
On going through the records and existence of the said business, the loan of Rs.15,00,000/-was sanctioned in the name of M/s.D.P.Foods.
The accused has submitted and under taken there is no any other liability in any other Bank either in his name or in the name of his company.
But however later the informant came to know that the accused has taken Home loan of Rs.70,00,000/- from other Bank on 03.11.2011.
The accused had suppressed this information and had obtained the loan.
The said loan was a Home loan and it was not mentioned in the audited Balance Sheet furnished by the accused.
Later, the accused has not paid any installment and the account was turned into NPA.
The Bank has issued Notice and started verifying the audited Balance Sheet furnished by the accused.
They came to know that the said Balance Sheet was fabricated and forged one.
It was not signed by the Chartered Accountant.
The accused with dishonest criminal intention to defraud and cheat the Nationalized Bank has fabricated and created the documents to avail loan to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- and acted criminally.
The informant had been to the police station and lodged the information.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the case was registered in Crime No.175/2015 at Jayanagar Police Station.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru City had filed Police Report against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to the accused.
He has appeared before this Court and executed bail bonds.
The copies of the Police Report and other Prosecution papers are furnished to the accused under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused has committed offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code has been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, the Prosecution has examined three witnesses PW1 to PW3 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P25.

After completion of the prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.
Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned Counsel for the accused.

5. The points for determination are;
1. Whether Prosecution has proved the offences charged against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt?
2. What order or sentence?

K Nagaraj vs Dayanandaprabhu on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136728134/
2 6.

My answers to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Negative, Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 7. POINT No.1 :- To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 K.Nagaraj, wherein, he has deposed that he was the Manager of Indian Bank, Jayanagar in between the period of January 2015 to August 2015.
The accused has availed the loan of Rs. 15,00,000 and he has not paid the installment regularly and his account was turned into NPA.
The accused has not continued his business and even he was not engaged in any other business.
The accused has purchased machinery from the loan taken by him from the informant Bank.
But he has sold all the machinery of his business.
His statement was recorded by the Police.
8. The Prosecution has examined CW2/PW2 W.R.Rajendran, wherein he has deposed that during the year 2011 of November, the accused had taken loan of Rs.15,00,000/-.
He has verified the records and more particularly the Assets and Liabilities furnished by the accused.
This witness has deposed he was informed by the accused that he was having a house loan, but he has not verified the records.
The accused has paid only the interest of Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs.2,50,000/-to the Bank.

Later,
he got transferred to some other Bank.
His statement was not recorded by the police.

9. This witness is cross-examined by the learned Counsel for the accused, wherein, he has admitted that the accused has not forged any documents and all the documents submitted by the accused are authenticated.
Before sanctioning the loan, he has taken the legal opinion and verified all all the records from the concerned Department.
The accused has paid the installments regularly.
This witness has deposed and admitted that he does not have any personal knowledge whether the accused has committed any fraud to the Bank.
10. The Prosecution has examined CW3/PW4 Jothsna Sahu, wherein she has deposed that she has verified the Records before sanctioning the loan to the accused.
This witness is cross-examined by the learned Counsel, wherein she has admitted that the NPA Notice was not issued to the accused.
This witness has deposed that, it is their duty to call the reports from all the Banks to ascertain whether this accused is having any loan in their Bank.
11. It is the case of the Prosecution that the accused has availed a loan of Rs.15,00,000/- in the name of his business M/s.D.P.Foods.
The accused has submitted the audited Balance Sheet for the year ending 31.03.2009, 31.03.2010 and 31.03.2011.
Later, the accused has not paid the said loan amount and the account was turned into NPA.
As per Ex.P1, it is the case of the Prosecution that the said Audited Balance Sheet forged by the accused and created to obtain loan.
It was not signed by the Chartered Accountant.

It is the burden of the Prosecution to show that the accused has created and forged the Audited Balance Sheet for the year ending 31.03.2009, 31.03.2010 and 31.03.2011.
12.
The Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1, wherein this witness has deposed only that the accused in the name of M/s.D.P.Foods has obtained the loan from the Bank.

But however he has not K Nagaraj vs Dayanandaprabhu on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136728134/
3 deposed whether the accused has forged the documents more particularly the audited report as alleged in the FIR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This witness has not at all deposed that the accused has forged the audited Balance Sheet for the year ending 31.03.2009, 31.03.2010 and 31.03.2011 to obtained the loan.
The only evidence of CW1 before this Court is that the loan taken by the accused was turned into NPA.
The accused has not repaid the loan.
This witness has deposed that the accused has found loss in his business and he has sold all the equipments of his business.
This accused has taken loan to purchase these equipments.
But, however this version is not at all found in Ex.P1.

PW2/CW2 W.R.Rajendran,
who is a Retired General Manager has deposed that his statement was not at all recorded by the IO.
This witness has confirmed that before sanctioning the loan, they have verified the entire Records and obtained Civil Report.
The said Civil Report was not a fake or forged by the accused.
This witness has deposed that the accused has not paid the installments in time.
CW4/PW3 has deposed that the accused account was turned as NPA.
Even, the Notice was not served to the accused.

This witness has not deposed anything about the forging of the document as alleged in her statement nor she has deposed about her statement alleged to be recorded by the Police during the course of investigation.
13.
The Prosecution has listed about 7 witnesses to prove the guilt of the accused.
My Predecessor has issued summons, warrants and Proclamation to the witnesses where in the Prosecution was not able to secure CW3 to CW7 who are the material witnesses to the case.
On perusal of the Order Sheet, it reveals that even after repeated issuance of warrants against CW3 to CW7, they were not secured and examined.
Hence, the said witnesses were dropped.
This case is pending since 2016 and the accused is regular before this Court.

Mere for the reason that the accused has not paid the installments, it cannot be termed that the accused has created and forged the documents and committed the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
The informant has filed this criminal case against the accused only for the reason that the accused has not paid the installments.
It is purely civil in nature and it is very unfortunate that the Criminal Case is registered against the accused.

Under these circumstances, I am holding that the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

14. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the accused is not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against him.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS
Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bond and surety bond executed under Section 437 of Cr.P.C. will be in force till appeal period and thereafter, it shall be canceled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court, today this the 14th day of August 2024)
(SAHEEL AHMED.S.KUNNIBHAVI) II Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
